extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and advanced geometry students (readers of 19th-century mathematical journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and proving geometric properties and optimization results for ellipses and conics (e.g., greatest inscribed and least circumscribed ellipse to a quadrilateral) using analytic geometry and classical constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose convenient coordinate axes
rubrics_metrics.description: Take lines through a vertex parallel to two sides (or take the diagonals for circumscribed problems) for coordinate axes so that equations of the sides and conics assume tractable forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for the inscribed-ellipse problem take axes through P parallel to SR and RQ; for circumscribed ellipse take diagonals PR, QS as axes. This simplifies writing the four side-equations (I–4) or the general conic (26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the ellipse / conic with general centered quadratic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Denote an ellipse (or general central conic) by a quadratic form in (x−h) and (y−k): a(y−k)^2 + 2b(x−h)(y−k) + c(x−h)^2 + ... = 0 (equation (5), (31)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use centered form with parameters a, b, c and centre (h,k); relate these parameters to tangency/passing-through conditions of the quadrilateral's sides or vertices via substitution and reduction (see equations (13)–(16) and (27)–(30)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangency conditions yield algebraic constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition that the four sides be tangents to the ellipse produces a set of algebraic equations relating a, b, c, h, k (e.g. equations (13)–(16)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive these by substituting the line-equations into the conic and equating the discriminant or matching coefficients so the line is tangent; these reduced relations are essential to determine the ellipse parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal semi-axes from extremal radius condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal semi-axes are the maxima/minima values of the radius r (with r^2 expressed as a quadratic in coordinates); hence differentiate the relation for r^2 subject to the conic equation and set the differential to zero to obtain the characteristic equation whose roots are r^2 (see (6)–(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply the differential of the radius relation by an arbitrary scalar X and add the differential of the constraint; eliminate differentials to get linear relations, then eliminate x−h, y−k to obtain a quadratic in r^2. The absolute term equals the product of squares of principal semi-axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area expressed via principal axes and extremization
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of the ellipse equals π times the product of the principal semi-axes, which can be obtained from the characteristic equation for r^2; maximize (inscribed) or minimize (circumscribed) this area by optimizing the corresponding algebraic expression in the parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inscribed ellipse the derived quadratic's absolute term (product of r^2 roots) gives area; require that the expression ae − b^2 (or ac − V in the text) be positive for a real ellipse. Differentiate the area-expression w.r.t. parameters (h,k, etc.) and solve for extrema (see (11), (12), (17)–(22)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check reality and geometric admissibility of algebraic roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic equations (quadratic, cubic) may yield multiple algebraic roots; one must discard roots giving imaginary areas or coefficients that make ac − V negative (i.e., yielding hyperbolas or non-real ellipses) and select the root that satisfies the intended geometric configuration (salient/intersectant/re-entrant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: expression (21) gives an imaginary area and is discarded; verify signs and positivity of auxiliary expressions (e.g., ae − V > 0) and whether the root corresponds to the salient quadrilateral case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish cases of quadrilateral configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment must consider salient (convex), re-entrant, and intersectant quadrilaterals separately because the same analytic equations may represent ellipses or hyperbolas depending on configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters p,q, etc., (and sign choices in formulas) correspond to different quadrilateral types; check which choice makes ae − V positive and which roots fulfill the geometric constraints (Scholium 2 discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus property for centers of conics tangent to a quadrilateral
rubrics_metrics.description: All conic sections which touch the sides (or their extensions) of a given quadrilateral have their centres situated on the straight line which bisects the diagonals of the quadrilateral (line (19)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a constraint: the centre (h,k) of any such conic must lie on that bisecting line, reducing unknowns when searching for inscribed/circumscribed conics.

rubrics_metrics.name: When minimizing circumscribed ellipse, solve resultant cubic and choose admissible root
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimization of the area of a circumscribed ellipse that passes through the four vertices leads to a cubic equation in a parameter (equation (33)); although there may be up to three real roots analytically, only the root that yields ac − V positive and the intended configuration is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute all roots, check which produce real ellipse coefficients and satisfy geometric conditions (e.g., salient quadrilateral), and discard others that correspond to hyperbolas or invalid configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use orthographic projection construction for dividing ellipse into equal sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide an ellipse into n equal sectors geometrically when a regular n-gon is constructible: project ellipse orthographically to a circle, inscribe a regular polygon, then project back to get division lines on the ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a circle orthographically related to the ellipse (choose inclination so axes align as required), inscribe regular n-gon in the circle, draw lines parallel to ellipse major/minor axes through polygon vertices to intersect ellipse and join to centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: General algebraic-elimination methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying analytic methods, combine differentials and constraints by multiplying by an arbitrary scalar (X) to eliminate differentials and unknowns, then eliminate variables systematically to obtain polynomial equations in the remaining parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technique is repeatedly used: differentiate constraint and target relation, multiply one by X, add, equate coefficients of differentials to zero, eliminate X (set X = −1/r^2), and reduce to polynomial in r^2 or other parameters (see derivations leading to (11), (33)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-of-semi-axes equals constant term of characteristic equation
rubrics_metrics.description: The absolute (constant) term of the characteristic polynomial obtained for r^2 equals the product of the squares of the principal semi-axes; this identifies the ellipse area algebraically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theory of equations: for the quadratic (or higher) in r^2 derived from extremal conditions, take its constant term (with sign) as the product of r1^2 r2^2 ... and hence compute area = π·(product of semi-axes)^(1/2).
